change: Qualified the typical rather than exceptionless preservation of truth conditions, added dislocation types, and retained absence of a well-formed basic counterpart in certain constructions.
Expanded the two-way taxonomy to include dislocation, distinguishing reordering from realignment and avoiding a claim of overt added material in every case.
Added §1 examples where a canonical alternative is syntactically or pragmatically unacceptable and clarified that process terms describe structural differences rather than literal transformations.

Qualified general combinability by the structural compatibility requirements for packaging subtypes: passive plus extraposition can combine, existential plus subject extraposition cannot under these definitions.
Recorded Chapter 16's demonstration that the relative scope of many and negation can differ between information-packaging alternants, potentially changing truth conditions.
Explicitly distinguished auxiliary–subject inversion from subject–dependent inversion as used in the Chapter 16 information-packaging overview.
